# Linux/Command Line Essentials {#sec-command-line}

## Navigation

```bash
# Where am I?
pwd

# List files
ls              # Basic list
ls -la          # Detailed list with hidden files
ls -lh          # Human-readable file sizes

# Change directory
cd /path/to/dir
cd ..           # Go up one level
cd ~            # Go to home directory
cd -            # Go to previous directory
```

## File Operations

```bash
# Create files
touch newfile.txt

# Create directories
mkdir -p path/to/new/dir

# Copy
cp file.txt backup.txt
cp -r directory/ backup/

# Move / rename
mv oldname.txt newname.txt

# Delete
rm file.txt
rm -r directory/    # Be careful!
```

## Viewing Files

```bash
# View entire file
cat file.txt

# View with line numbers
cat -n file.txt

# View beginning
head file.txt           # First 10 lines
head -20 file.txt       # First 20 lines

# View end
tail file.txt           # Last 10 lines
tail -20 file.txt       # Last 20 lines

# View interactively
less file.txt           # Space to page, q to quit
```

## Searching

```bash
# Search for text in files
grep "ATG" sequences.fasta
grep -i "atg" sequences.fasta    # Case insensitive
grep -c "ATG" sequences.fasta    # Count matches
grep -n "ATG" sequences.fasta    # Show line numbers
grep -r "ATG" directory/         # Recursive search

# Find files
find . -name "*.fasta"
find . -name "*.py" -size +1k
find . -type f -mtime -7         # Modified in last 7 days
```

## Text Processing

```bash
# Count lines, words, characters
wc file.txt
wc -l file.txt          # Just lines

# Sort
sort file.txt
sort -n file.txt        # Numeric sort
sort -k2 file.txt       # Sort by second column

# Unique lines
sort file.txt | uniq

# Extract columns
cut -f1,3 file.txt      # Tab-delimited columns 1 and 3
cut -d',' -f2 file.csv  # Comma-delimited column 2

# Replace text
sed 's/ATG/XXX/g' file.txt    # Replace all ATG with XXX
sed -i 's/ATG/XXX/g' file.txt # In-place edit
```

## Pipes and Redirection

```bash
# Pipe output to another command
cat sequences.fasta | grep ">" | wc -l

# Redirect to file
echo "ATGCG" > output.txt       # Overwrite
echo "GCTAG" >> output.txt      # Append

# Redirect stderr
command 2> error.log
command > output.txt 2>&1       # Both stdout and stderr
```

## Process Management

```bash
# List running processes
ps aux

# Kill a process
kill PID
kill -9 PID             # Force kill

# Run in background
command &

# Check background jobs
jobs
```

## File Permissions

```bash
# View permissions
ls -la

# Make executable
chmod +x script.py

# Read/write for owner only
chmod 600 file.txt
```

## Environment Variables

```bash
# View all env vars
env

# Set a variable
export MY_VAR="value"

# Use a variable
echo $MY_VAR

# Make permanent (add to ~/.bashrc)
echo 'export MY_VAR="value"' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc
```

## Useful Shortcuts

```bash
# Tab completion
# Press Tab to auto-complete file names and commands

# Command history
history             # Show command history
!42                 # Run command #42
!!                  # Run last command
!grep               # Run last command starting with grep

# Ctrl+C            # Cancel current command
# Ctrl+D            # Exit shell
# Ctrl+R            # Search command history
# Ctrl+L            # Clear screen
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Practice

The best way to learn the command line is to use it. Try these exercises:

1. Navigate to a directory and list all `.py` files
2. Count how many lines are in a FASTA file
3. Find all sequences containing "ATG" in a file
4. Sort a file by the second column
:::
